create.name: Kelly Boys
create.bio:
Kelly Boys is a mindfulness trainer, coach and writer whose teaching now centres on yoga nidra, the lying-down guided practice she often presents under the modern name non-sleep deep rest. She studied intercultural religious studies, trained and certified as a teacher of the iRest form of yoga nidra, and for a time ran operations at the institute behind it, co-leading its teacher trainings and retreats. She later directed the global facilitator training of Search Inside Yourself, the mindfulness and emotional intelligence programme that began at Google, and co-designed a mindfulness and wellbeing course for United Nations humanitarian staff that is now used across several UN agencies.

Her guided practices are short and plain-spoken: a body scan, a few minutes of welcoming whatever feelings are present, a pause to rest between tasks. They have found a wide audience on her YouTube channel and on several meditation apps. Alongside the practices she offers one-to-one coaching built around the ideas of her book The Blind Spot Effect, which looks at the habits of perception and belief that we cannot easily see in ourselves, and she leads deep rest retreats at centres including Esalen. She is writing a second book on deep rest.

books.title: The Blind Spot Effect: How to Stop Missing What's Right in Front of You
books.author: Kelly Boys
books.description: A practical look at the gaps in how we perceive, feel and think, drawing on psychology and neuroscience. Each chapter has exercises for noticing hidden beliefs and habits, from snap judgements to patterns in close relationships.

courses.title: Blind Spots Coaching
courses.description: One-to-one coaching sessions that look at the unseen beliefs and needs behind patterns that keep repeating at work or in relationships, using the approach of her book.

free_resources.title: 21-Day Rest & Reset Protocol
free_resources.description: A free download given to newsletter subscribers: a short booklet on deep rest practice and two new guided recordings, with a plan for practising daily over three weeks.
